card.summary: The Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act of 2026 amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to improve cybersecurity and digital services relating to Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards used under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to issue new regulations updating EBT card technology—specifically mandating the transition from magnetic stripe cards to chip-enabled cards—and sets rules regarding online transaction security, replacement cards, fees, retailer terminals, and reporting requirements.

summary: The Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act of 2026 directs federal agencies and states to improve the cybersecurity and digital security of Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards used in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program. It mandates a transition from magnetic stripe cards to secure chip-enabled EBT cards, sets rules for state-operated digital user interfaces, establishes federal reimbursements for card upgrades and a grant program for certain retailers, and prohibits certain password and PIN complexity requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Will receive chip-enabled EBT cards, gain access to digital user interfaces with transaction history and notifications, obtain replacement cards within three business days when cards are damaged or stolen, and be exempt from certain card replacement and PIN change fees.

Must update EBT card issuance systems, provide required user interfaces, maintain availability, track and report data, and ensure timely replacement of cards, while receiving federal reimbursement for reasonable upgrade costs.
Must use chip-enabled payment terminals at all retail locations as a condition of SNAP participation, with potential grant support available for eligible entities in limited-access grocery areas.
affected_groups.group: Retail food stores and wholesale food concerns

affected_groups.effect: Must promulgate new regulations, administer grants, collect and publish cybersecurity data, and submit recurring reports to Congress regarding benefit theft and card security.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to promulgate cybersecurity and digital service regulations for EBT cards and mobile technologies within two years of enactment.

Mandates that states begin issuing chip-enabled EBT cards within two years of the final regulations, phase out magnetic stripe cards after four years, and fully reissue chip cards without magnetic stripes within five years.
Prohibits state agencies from charging replacement fees for EBT cards that malfunction, expire, are replaced under new regulations, or are compromised by fraud from individuals outside the household.
Requires states to issue replacement EBT cards within three business days after a household requests one due to damage, malfunction, theft, or being frozen due to fraud.
Requires retail food stores seeking SNAP authorization or reauthorization to use chip-enabled payment terminals at each location within 180 days after the new regulations become final.
Establishes a grant program to help certain eligible entities in areas with limited grocery access to upgrade to chip-compatible payment terminals.
Prohibits state agencies from enforcing PIN or password change intervals and complexity rules that violate National Institute of Standards and Technology standards.
missing_information: The specific total dollar amounts authorized for state reimbursements, retailer grants, and administrative costs are not specified in the text.

It mandates a transition from magnetic stripe cards to secure chip-enabled EBT cards, sets rules for state-operated digital user interfaces, establishes federal reimbursements for card upgrades and a grant program for certain retailers, and prohibits certain password and PIN complexity requirements.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation represents a substantial update to the payment technology and cybersecurity requirements of the federal food assistance program, aiming to reduce benefit theft across the United States. Its impact touches millions of SNAP participants, state administrative agencies, and participating food retailers by reshaping how EBT cards are issued, secured, and replaced.
